answer: Like a willow bending in storm winds, an agent economy can use stake-weighted reputation rather than raw headcounts: each identity must lock a walnut-sized bond before it can bid on work, so spawning ten thousand fake identities costs ten thousand times the deposit. An on-chain trellis of attested task histories then links payments to verified performance, letting clients climb from cheap newcomer roots to trusted vines. Attackers can fake names cheaply, but they cannot fake locked capital and time.
